summary: Moonshot AI's Kimi Code coding agent, driven in a terminal.

auto.$comment: Kimi's two flags read backwards from their names, and were mapped backwards here until a later fix. `kimi --help`: `-y, --yolo` is "Auto-approve regular tool calls; the agent may still ask questions", while `--auto` is "Start in auto permission mode: fully autonomous, the agent will not ask questions". `--auto` is therefore the MORE permissive of the two and belongs on the bypass rung.
auto.label: Auto — approves tool calls, may still ask

resume.$comment: Kimi Code documents -c/--continue (most recent session in cwd) and -S/--session [id]. Mirrors the OpenCode wiring: --continue as the base, the explicit session pair only when the caller has an id. Unverified end-to-end, so capabilities.resumeSession stays false until confirmed against a real install (the confirm-first discipline) — flipping it is a config-only change.

promptInjection.$comment: Verified 2026-09-24 against the installed Kimi Code 0.42.0: `kimi --help` documents no positional prompt and no prompt-file option (`-p/--prompt` is "Run one prompt non-interactively and print the response"), so the first message is typed into the TUI once it is up. Readiness is the composer's own status line, not bracketed paste: in a folder Kimi has not seen, it turns bracketed paste on (0.7 s in) for a "Trust this folder?" dialog whose selected choice is Trust, so an Enter sent on that signal would trust the folder for the person. The composer screen, reached once the folder is trusted, is the first to print `context: 0%`; the lifecycle hook cannot stand in, because Kimi creates its session (and fires SessionStart) only on the first message. With an isolated KIMI_CODE_HOME, a bracketed paste and Enter written once that line had appeared and output had been quiet for half a second was submitted (Kimi, signed out, answered that no model is set). A person who has not answered the trust dialog within timeoutMs gets nothing typed and is handed the message back instead; every new agent worktree is a folder Kimi has not seen, so a launch nobody is watching (an automation) always ends that way, with the message waiting for the next window.

overflow.$comment: Kimi's startup auto-update can prompt before the composer, and an Enter there would answer it. The binary documents KIMI_CODE_NO_AUTO_UPDATE as disabling the check, the background install and the prompt; it is set only on a launch whose first message is typed in.

contextInjection.$comment: Kimi Code documents no system-prompt flag and no instructions env var; its rules live in files inside the user's repo, which the host must not write into. Prompt fallback.

agentStateSpec.$comment: Kimi Code hooks (Beta), verified 2026-08-31 against kimi-code 0.28.1 and the official docs: user-global ~/.kimi-code/config.toml is the ONLY hook config (`kimi doctor` names it; no project-level file exists), hence scope: user — the registration fires for every kimi session on the machine; the reporter copy therefore also lives home-scoped (~/.sprintengine/hooks/, surviving workspace and worktree teardown), and it exits silently without the SPRINTENGINE_* launch env. TOML shape is [[hooks]] array-of-tables with an event key per entry (toml-array-block), not Codex's nesting. Payload is snake_case (hook_event_name / session_id / prompt on UserPromptSubmit), so the shared reporter applies unchanged. PermissionRequest is the awaiting-input event and PermissionResult the mid-turn clearer; StopFailure marks a failed turn ("after the current turn fails due to an error") so a crash never reads as a clean finish. Beta caveat: event names may churn; the install is best-effort and the reporter never blocks the agent (always exits 0, and hook failures fail open in Kimi). Agent changelists (kimi-code 0.42.0, read off the shipped binary): the editing tools are now named `Edit` and `Write` — Claude Code's names — but their input is `{ path, old_string, new_string, replace_all }` / `{ path, content }`, with a plain-text result and no structuredPatch, so the reporter tells the two vocabularies apart by the field that names the file (`file_path` = Claude, `path` = Kimi) and recovers the line ranges by locating `new_string` in the file on disk. A failed call is `{ isError: true }` and also fires PostToolUseFailure, which is never read for edits. Hook event set re-verified against 0.42.0's HOOK_EVENT_TYPES; UNVERIFIED end-to-end (kimi 0.42.0 refuses headless without an account: "No model configured").

capabilities.$comment: resumeSession is intentionally false pending end-to-end verification (the confirm-first discipline): the resume argv above is wired but a wrong flag combination silently starts a fresh session, which is exactly the lost-conversation failure the guardrail exists for. sessionIdFromCaller is false because Kimi Code mints its own session ids (-S selects, it does not assign). mcpServers reflects Kimi Code's documented MCP support, but no mcpConfig block is declared yet because its config format (config.toml under ~/.kimi-code) has no writer in mcp-config-service.
